name: Lunda
notes: Standard Chilunda (Lunda) Latin orthography, standardized by Zambia's Ministry of Education in 1977 alongside Bemba, Nyanja, Tonga, Lozi, Kaonde and Luvale (the seven official Zambian regional languages; Lunda is also one of the recognized national/trade languages of Zambia's North-Western Province, shared with communities in the DR Congo and Angola). Five-vowel system /a e i o u/ with phonemic length written by doubling the vowel letter (⟨aa⟩ = /aː/, etc. — a geminate-vowel spelling for one long nucleus, the pattern documented for Garifuna in cab.json, AGENTS.md test 2). ⟨ch⟩ and ⟨j⟩ spell the single affricates /t̠ʃ/ and /d̠ʒ/, ⟨sh⟩ and ⟨zh⟩ the fricatives /ʃ/ /ʒ/, ⟨ny⟩ the palatal nasal /ɲ/ — none the concatenation of their parts (AGENTS.md test 1). ⟨ng'⟩ (with a following apostrophe) spells the plain velar nasal /ŋ/, the same disambiguating convention documented for Zambian Tonga and Lozi under the shared 1977 harmonized orthography, blocking the wrong maximal-munch read as ⟨n⟩+⟨g⟩ (AGENTS.md test 3). Retained from the prior stub: intervocalic ⟨d⟩ has a fricative allophone [ʒ], ⟨l⟩ an [n] allophone, ⟨t⟩ a [t̠ʃ] allophone before front vowels, and ⟨z⟩ a [d̠ʒ] allophone — all cited in the PHOIBLE-sourced inventory. Smoke-tested against the shared Bantu Zambian-cluster infinitive prefix ku- (e.g. Luvale ⟨kutonga⟩ 'to sew') confirming the k-u onset-vowel segments resolve consistently across the harmonized-orthography sibling languages. Lunda is tonal with no lexical word stress; tone is not consistently marked in ordinary orthography and is left unencoded here, a documented exemption distinct from stress (docs/quality_tiers.md).
